sentences.ko: 결혼 생활 유지하는 게 얼마나 힘든 건지 넌 진짜 몰라.
sentences.text: You have no idea what it takes to make a marriage work.

alts.text: Trust me, you've got no clue how hard staying married really is.
I do not think you understand how much effort a marriage requires.

sentences.note: **what it takes to** 는 '그게 되게 하려면 무엇이 있어야 하는지'라는 뜻입니다. 상대가 어떤 일을 쉽게 말할 때 '너는 그게 얼마나 힘든지 모른다'고 받아치는 자리에서 **have no idea** 와 짝으로 잘 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너희는 왜 우리랑 한 번도 포커 안 쳤어?
sentences.text: HOW COME YOU GUYS HAVE NEVER PLAYED poker with us?

alts.text: Seriously, how come you've never played poker with us?
May I ask why you have never joined us for a game of poker?

sentences.note: **how come** 은 why 와 뜻이 같지만 뒤에 문장을 그대로 붙입니다(how come you've ~ , 'do you' 처럼 뒤집지 않습니다). 친한 사이에 '왜 여태 안 그랬어?' 하고 가볍게 물을 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 걔가 그거 볼까 봐 동네를 다 돌면서 파는 데 있는 대로 다 사버렸어.
sentences.text: Yeah, I didn't want her to see it, so I ran around the neighborhood and bought all the copies I could find.

alts.text: No way was I letting her see it, so I grabbed every copy in the neighborhood.
To prevent her from seeing it, I went around the neighborhood and purchased every copy that was available.

sentences.note: **all the copies I could find** 처럼 <all the + 명사 + I could + 동사>는 '내가 구할 수 있는 건 하나도 안 남기고 다'라는 뜻입니다. 힘 닿는 데까지 다 했다고 말할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이제야 진짜 떠난다는 게 실감 나나 봐. 좀 울컥해 있으니까 괜히 건드리는 말 하지 마.
sentences.text: Now, it just hit her that she's leaving and she's kind of emotional, so no one say anything to set her off.

alts.text: She's only just realizing she's actually going, so nobody say anything that'll set her off.
The reality of her departure has finally sunk in, so please avoid saying anything that might upset her.

sentences.note: **it just hit her that** 는 '이제야 실감이 났다'는 뜻으로, 머리로는 알던 일이 갑자기 와닿을 때 씁니다. **set her off** 는 울음이나 화를 터뜨리게 만든다는 뜻이라 예민한 사람 앞에서 '건드리지 마'라고 할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이 케이크 망치고 싶었으면 내가 직접 구웠지.
sentences.text: All right, IF I WANTED THIS CAKE to be a disaster, I WOULD HAVE BAKED IT MYSELF.

alts.text: Hey, if I'd wanted a disaster, I'd have baked it myself.
Had I wanted this cake to be a failure, I would have baked it myself.

sentences.note: **I would have baked it myself** 처럼 <if + 과거, would have p.p.>는 '그럴 작정이었으면 이렇게 했지'라며 농담조로 자기를 낮출 때 씁니다. 사 오거나 시킨 것을 두고 누가 흠을 잡을 때 받아치는 말투입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 야, 너 이제 건강 엄청 챙기는 그런 사람 되려는 거야?
sentences.text: So, you're going to be one of those healthy, healthy, healthy guys?

alts.text: Wait, are you turning into one of those health nuts now?
Are you planning to become one of those very health-conscious people?

sentences.note: **one of those** 는 상대를 어떤 부류로 묶어서 놀리듯 말할 때 씁니다. 운동이나 식단을 갑자기 챙기기 시작한 친구에게 쓰기 좋고, 더 편한 자리에서는 **health nuts** 라고 부릅니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그러니까, 너 걔랑 결혼하는 모습이 그려지냐고.
sentences.text: I mean, like, do you see yourself marrying her?

alts.text: Can you honestly picture yourself marrying her?
Do you imagine yourself marrying her someday?

sentences.note: **do you see yourself** 는 "앞으로 그런 모습이 상상이 되냐"고 물을 때 쓰는 말입니다. 진로나 결혼처럼 먼 미래를 떠볼 때 자주 나오고, **picture yourself** 로 바꿔 써도 같은 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내가 이 승진을 받아들이면, 이게 진짜 내 일이라고 인정하는 꼴이 되잖아.
sentences.text: If I took this promotion, it would be like admitting that this is what I actually do.

alts.text: Taking the promotion would basically mean I'm admitting this is really my job.
Accepting this promotion would be an admission that this is what I actually do for a living.

sentences.note: **it would be like admitting** 은 "그렇게 하면 사실상 무엇을 인정하는 셈이 된다"고 말할 때 씁니다. 하기 싫은 선택 앞에서 이유를 댈 때 쓰기 좋고, 더 편하게는 **would basically mean** 으로 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저기, 그때 내가 더 힘이 되어 주지 못해서 정말 미안해.
sentences.text: You know, I'm I'm really sorry I wasn't more supportive before.

alts.text: Hey, sorry I wasn't there for you more back then.
I would like to apologize for not being more supportive at the time.

sentences.note: **supportive** 는 곁에서 응원하고 편이 되어 주는 것을 말합니다. 지난 일을 뒤늦게 사과할 때 쓰고, 말할 때는 **there for you** 가 더 흔합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: So, isn't it a bit cold out for shorts?

alts.text: Aren't you freezing in those shorts?
Is the weather not a little too cold for shorts?

sentences.note: **cold out** 의 out 은 "바깥 날씨가"라는 뜻입니다. 옷차림을 두고 한마디 할 때 **too cold for shorts** 처럼 "~하기엔 너무 춥다" 형태로 쓰고, a bit 을 넣으면 지적이 부드러워집니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends
